groups.title: E-commerce Architecture Concepts
groups.question: You are building a JAMstack shop with products in a CMS, a cart and Stripe payments. Explain how you would model products, keep the cart and take payment.

followUps.Product catalogue modelling in a headles: How would you model products and their variants in a CMS?
followUps.Cart state management with Context API o: Where should cart state live so it survives page changes and reloads?
followUps.Stripe payment intents and the checkout: How does a Stripe Checkout Session work?

evidence.text: Products are content types with fields like name, description, price and images.
Variants like size or colour are modelled as linked entries or structured fields.
Prices used for payment should come from a trusted source, not from the browser.

notEnough: Only saying you add products to the CMS.

evidence.text: The cart lives in a context or store above the routes so it survives navigation.
Saving it to localStorage restores it after a reload.
A small store like Zustand avoids re-rendering everything when the cart changes.
The server creates a Checkout Session with the items to pay for.
Stripe returns a URL to a hosted payment page.
After payment, Stripe redirects to your success page with the session id.

groups.title: Webhooks and Order Processing
groups.question: Customers sometimes close the browser right after paying and never reach the success page, so orders go unrecorded. Explain how you would process orders reliably.

followUps.Stripe webhooks for reliable post-paymen: Why use a webhook instead of the success page to record orders?
followUps.Order confirmation emails with serverles: How would you send an order confirmation email after payment?

evidence.text: Stripe sends a signed request to your function when a payment completes.
It arrives even if the customer closes the browser.
Verifying the signature proves the request really came from Stripe.
The webhook handler triggers the email after a successful payment.
An email service like SendGrid or Resend sends it.
The handler should avoid sending the same email twice if the webhook is retried.

notEnough: Only saying you send an email.

groups.title: Stripe Integration Tooling
groups.question: You are integrating Stripe in the browser and testing payments locally. Explain how to load Stripe on the client and test webhooks without real payments.

followUps.Stripe JS SDK and stripe-js client-side: Why load Stripe.js from Stripe's own servers?
followUps.Stripe CLI for local webhook testing and: How does the Stripe CLI help you test webhooks locally?

evidence.text: The stripe-js package loads Stripe.js asynchronously.
Stripe.js provides payment elements where customers enter card details.
Card details go directly to Stripe, which keeps your site out of most PCI requirements.

notEnough: Only saying you install the package.

evidence.text: stripe listen forwards webhook events to your local function.
stripe trigger sends test events on demand.
You can test the full flow without real payments.

notEnough: Only saying it is a command-line tool.

groups.title: Dynamic Data and Serverless Checkout
groups.question: Your checkout function builds a Stripe session from the cart, and the success page should show the order details. Explain how both work securely.

followUps.Creating Stripe Checkout Sessions in ser: Why must the function build line items from your own prices, not prices from the browser?
followUps.Reading Stripe session data on the succe: How does the success page show the confirmed order?

evidence.text: A serverless function uses the Stripe SDK to create the session.
Prices must come from your product data, because the browser can be tampered with.
The function returns the session URL for the client to redirect to.

notEnough: Only saying the function creates a session.

evidence.text: Stripe adds the session id to the success URL.
The page asks a serverless function to retrieve that session from Stripe.
It shows the confirmed order details from Stripe's data, not from the client.

notEnough: Only saying it reads the URL.
